title: Low-precision fallback throttle and kernel-mismatch stability action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After a weekend incident where low-precision (int4/int3) serving paths triggered a restart spiral on a small subset of Dedicated hosts, we ran a targeted investigation. The symptom was a sudden uptick in per-GPU restarts and degraded accuracy on RLHF chat models when the runtime attempted to auto-fallback between kernel variants under load. This ticket tracks remediation work: short-term mitigations to stop customer-visible outages and a set of long-term engineering changes to prevent recurrence and detect regressions earlier.
impact_summary: ~42 Dedicated hosts experienced repeated process restarts across 2026-03-07 03:00–08:30 UTC. Affected customers saw increased 5xxs and accuracy drift (measured BLEU-like surrogate and client QA test failures) for int3/int4 pinned variants. Rolling canaries missed the failure because the specific traffic mix (high prefix reuse + heavy KV-cache churn) was underrepresented in canary samples.
timeline: 2026-03-07 02:50 UTC: first elevated restarts alerted via host-monitoring. 2026-03-07 03:10 UTC: automated fallback engaged across several pools. 2026-03-07 03:30 UTC: on-call isolated correlation to low-precision kernel selection and KV-cache eviction spikes. 2026-03-07 04:20 UTC: temporary mitigation applied (throttle auto-fallback to low-precision for affected pools). 2026-03-07 09:00 UTC: full rollback of recent kernel selection tuning and manual drain of unstable hosts. 2026-03-10: retrospective and investigation kickoff.
root_cause: Intermittent kernel-compat mismatch when switching between quantized kernel variants under high KV-cache churn. Two contributing issues: 1) a scheduling window allowed mixed-kernel execution that assumed API-level op semantics identical across variants; subtle dequant ordering differences introduced rare nondeterministic states leading to mutex contention and oom-like behaviors; 2) canary traffic did not exercise the high prefix-reuse + eviction pattern, so the regression slipped past rollout gates.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Blocked auto-fallback to low-precision kernels for model families with known op-surface differences for the next 4 releases. 2) Added a runtime guard: detect op-semantic mismatch signatures and fast-fail to stable FP16 variants without restarting the worker. 3) Expanded canary sampling to include prefix-heavy synthetic traces and KV-cache churn scenarios. 4) Emergency hotpatch to revert the kernel selector change that widened mixed-kernel windows.
long_term_action_items: Implement operator-level fingerprint testing in nightly CI to detect op-surface divergence between quantized and full-precision kernels.
Introduce a transactional kernel-swap protocol that drains in-flight KV-cache references before switching to a different kernel variant.
Add telemetry: per-request kernel-path annotations, prefix-reuse ratio, and KV-cache eviction counters tied to request IDs for post-incident tracing.
Create a canary workload suite that includes RLHF and chat-like sessions with heavy prefix reuse, to be run against every kernel and quantization change.
Formalize safe-fallback policies: per-model family policy config that defines allowed fallback targets and throttle thresholds.
Dedicated QA matrix for int3/int4 conversions including randomized operator reorder stress tests and concurrency fuzzing.
Schedule a cross-team design review (Runtime, KV-cache, Model-Onboarding) to align on kernel ABI guarantees and gating criteria for auto-quant rollout.
updates: 2026-03-10: Investigation started. Reproduced restart spiral locally with a crafted workload that forces rapid KV-cache evictions and mixed kernel swaps.
2026-03-11: Hotpatch deployed to block auto-fallback in affected pools (monitoring shows stabilizing host restarts).
2026-03-12: Canary sampling updated; new synthetic traces added to nightly canary harness. One additional kernel selector regression detected and reverted in staging.
2026-03-13: Draft of long-term action items reviewed by Runtime and QA teams; scheduling cross-team design review for 2026-03-24.
2026-03-13: Alerting playbook updated with a new 'kernel-mismatch' signature and runbook entries for fast-fail toggles.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keeping aggressive auto-fallback improves cost but increases risk when kernel semantics diverge; agreed to prefer safety-first for model families with high-regret accuracy profiles. QA will need extra cycles to expand conversion test coverage; plan includes a two-week runway to add operator fingerprinting and a longer runway (quarter) for transactional kernel swaps.
